statement: A *Gorenstein local ring* is a Noetherian local ring of finite injective dimension as a module over itself; a scheme $T$ is *Gorenstein* if it is locally Noetherian and all its local rings are Gorenstein. A complex in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *derived-invertible* if it has a two-sided derived tensor inverse, equivalently it is locally a shift of a line bundle. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ whose fibres are locally Noetherian, *Gorenstein at $x$* means that $f$ is flat at $x$ and the local ring of $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Gorenstein; *Gorenstein morphism* means this condition at every point. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be morphisms such that *all* fibres of $f,g,g\circ f$ are locally Noetherian. Then (1) if $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $g$ at $f(x)$, $g\circ f$ is Gorenstein at $x$; (2) if $f$ and $g$ are Gorenstein everywhere, then $g\circ f$ is Gorenstein; (3) if $g\circ f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $f$ is flat at $x$, then $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $g$ at $f(x)$; (4) if $g\circ f$ is Gorenstein everywhere and $f$ flat everywhere, then $f$ is Gorenstein everywhere and $g$ is Gorenstein **at points in the image of $f$**, not necessarily outside that image.
hypotheses: Three locally Noetherian fibre systems; additional flatness of f for converse directions.
conclusions: Four precise composition and descent implications for Gorenstein morphisms.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-composition-gorenstein}
Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be morphisms. Assume that the
fibres $X_y$, $Y_z$ and $X_z$ of $f$, $g$, and $g \circ f$ are
locally Noetherian.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $g$ is Gorenstein
at $f(x)$, then $g \circ f$ is Gorenstein at $x$.
\item If $f$ and $g$ are Gorenstein, then $g \circ f$ is Gorenstein.
\item If $g \circ f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $f$ is flat at $x$,
then $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ and $g$ is Gorenstein at $f(x)$.
\item If $g \circ f$ is Gorenstein and $f$ is flat, then
$f$ is Gorenstein and $g$ is Gorenstein at every point in
the image of $f$.
\end{enumerate}

statement: A *Gorenstein local ring* is a Noetherian local ring of finite injective dimension as a module over itself; a scheme $T$ is *Gorenstein* if it is locally Noetherian and all its local rings are Gorenstein. A complex in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *derived-invertible* if it has a two-sided derived tensor inverse, equivalently it is locally a shift of a line bundle. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ whose fibres are locally Noetherian, *Gorenstein at $x$* means that $f$ is flat at $x$ and the local ring of $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Gorenstein; *Gorenstein morphism* means this condition at every point. Form a cartesian square $X'=X\times_Y Y'\xrightarrow{g'}X$ over $g:Y'\to Y$, where the fibres of $f:X\to Y$ are locally Noetherian and $g$ is *locally of finite type*. Choose $x'\in X'$ mapping to $x\in X$, with $y'=f'(x')$, $y=f(x)$. Then: (1) if $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$, its pullback $f'$ is Gorenstein at $x'$; (2) if $f$ is flat at $x$ and $f'$ Gorenstein at $x'$, then $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$; (3) if $g$ is flat at $y'$ and $f'$ is Gorenstein at $x'$, then $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ (flatness of $f$ need not be separately assumed). No assertion that $g$ is globally flat is needed in (3).
hypotheses: f fibres locally Noetherian and g locally finite type; pointwise flatness extras by cases.
conclusions: Three base-change ascent and descent implications for pointwise Gorensteinness.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-base-change-gorenstein}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
Assume that all the fibres $X_y$ are locally Noetherian schemes.
Let $Y' \to Y$ be locally of finite type. Let $f' : X' \to Y'$
be the base change of $f$.
Let $x' \in X'$ be a point with image $x \in X$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$, then
$f' : X' \to Y'$ is Gorenstein at $x'$.
\item If $f$ is flat at $x$ and $f'$ is Gorenstein at $x'$, then $f$
is Gorenstein at $x$.
\item If $Y' \to Y$ is flat at $f'(x')$ and $f'$ is Gorenstein at
$x'$, then $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$.
\end{enumerate}

review_note: At line 6504 the pinned theorem assumes flat f in FTS_S and equates Gorenstein at x with f^!O_Y derived-invertible in some neighbourhood, yielding openness of the Gorenstein locus. The reconstruction keeps the local—not global—criterion and derived invertibility.
statement: A *Gorenstein local ring* is a Noetherian local ring of finite injective dimension as a module over itself; a scheme $T$ is *Gorenstein* if it is locally Noetherian and all its local rings are Gorenstein. A complex in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *derived-invertible* if it has a two-sided derived tensor inverse, equivalently it is locally a shift of a line bundle. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ whose fibres are locally Noetherian, *Gorenstein at $x$* means that $f$ is flat at $x$ and the local ring of $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Gorenstein; *Gorenstein morphism* means this condition at every point. Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and the category $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ of separated finite-type $S$-schemes. For $f:X\to Y$ therein, let $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ be the upper-shriek functor built from the right adjoint to proper pushforward on a compactification $X\hookrightarrow\bar X\to Y$. In particular $f^!\mathcal O_Y$ is a coherent bounded complex when $f$ is perfect. Let $f:X\to Y$ be flat in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ and $x\in X$. Then $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$ iff there exists an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq X$ of $x$ on which $f^!\mathcal O_Y|_U$ is **derived-invertible**, i.e. locally isomorphic to a shift of a line bundle. In particular the pointwise Gorenstein locus is open. This relative criterion uses the upper-shriek *complex*, not just its zeroth cohomology.
conclusions: Gorenstein at x iff f^!O_Y derived-invertible around x; locus open.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-affine-flat-Noetherian-gorenstein}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism
of $\textit{FTS}_S$. Let $x \in X$. If $f$ is flat, then
the following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$,
\item $f^!\mathcal{O}_Y$ is isomorphic to an invertible object
in a neighbourhood of $x$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, the set of points where $f$ is Gorenstein is
open in $X$.

statement: A *Gorenstein local ring* is a Noetherian local ring of finite injective dimension as a module over itself; a scheme $T$ is *Gorenstein* if it is locally Noetherian and all its local rings are Gorenstein. A complex in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *derived-invertible* if it has a two-sided derived tensor inverse, equivalently it is locally a shift of a line bundle. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ whose fibres are locally Noetherian, *Gorenstein at $x$* means that $f$ is flat at $x$ and the local ring of $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Gorenstein; *Gorenstein morphism* means this condition at every point. Let $f:X\to S$ be flat and locally of finite presentation, choose $x\in X$ and $s=f(x)$, and let $d=\dim_x(X_s)$ be the local topological dimension of the fibre. The following are equivalent: (1) $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$; (2) there is an open $U\ni x$ and a morphism $g:U\to\mathbf A^d_S$ locally quasi-finite over $S$ that is Gorenstein at $x$; (3) such an open $U$ exists with $g$ a Gorenstein morphism everywhere on $U$; (4) for **every** $S$-morphism $g:U\to\mathbf A^d_S$ defined on an open neighbourhood $U\ni x$, if $g$ is quasi-finite at $x$, then $g$ is Gorenstein at $x$. Here 'locally quasi-finite' does not automatically mean quasi-compact or globally quasi-finite. Consequently the Gorenstein locus of $f$ is open.
hypotheses: f flat lfp, x∈X with fibre-local dimension d, morphisms to relative affine d-space as specified.
conclusions: Four equivalent pointwise relative Gorenstein criteria and openness.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-finite-presentation-characterize-gorenstein}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is flat and locally
of finite presentation. Let $x \in X$ with image $s \in S$.
Set $d = \dim_x(X_s)$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is Gorenstein at $x$,
\item there exists an open neighbourhood $U \subset X$ of $x$
and a locally quasi-finite morphism $U \to \mathbf{A}^d_S$ over $S$
which is Gorenstein at $x$,
\item there exists an open neighbourhood $U \subset X$ of $x$
and a locally quasi-finite Gorenstein morphism $U \to \mathbf{A}^d_S$ over $S$,
\item for any $S$-morphism $g : U \to \mathbf{A}^d_S$
of an open neighbourhood $U \subset X$ of $x$ we have:
$g$ is quasi-finite at $x$ $\Rightarrow$ $g$ is Gorenstein at $x$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, the set of points where $f$ is Gorenstein is open in $X$.
